headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API egress and secret handling create leakage/compliance risk; Dagster adds little isolation and no direct interaction evidence is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem write, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly inject instructions into RD-Agent. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of outputs into RD-Agent’s browser/API-driven workflow, which is unusual and limited. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, uncertainty stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Dagster output into RD-Agent prompts or browser inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file or message channel is added between the agents, the pathway widens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy untrusted Dagster text into RD-Agent prompts.
Disable browser automation for RD-Agent during handoff tests.
Use a human-reviewed template for any transferred text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, logs, and competition datasets and can call external APIs. There is no documented shared workspace, but if Dagster outputs are fed into RD-Agent, sensitive content can leave the local boundary through RD-Agent’s broad egress. The interaction is inferred, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs contain sensitive operational data and are forwarded into RD-Agent, leakage can occur.
IF RD-Agent is configured to send prompts or context to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, or Kaggle APIs, those contents may leave the environment.
mitigations: Avoid passing sensitive Dagster artifacts into RD-Agent.
Redact logs and reports before any handoff.
Restrict RD-Agent API keys to non-sensitive test runs.
Review outbound API destinations in RD-Agent config.
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering before RD-Agent egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git, or use subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with RD-Agent in the documented profiles. RD-Agent can support multiple instances and writes logs, but without Dagster write access there is no meaningful shared-write conflict. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited to low-risk overlap at most.
conditions: IF Dagster is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants it write access, conflict risk increases.
IF both agents are later pointed at the same mutable directory, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep Dagster read-only in shared environments.
Separate log directories per agent.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
Run RD-Agent instances with distinct output paths.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is a data orchestrator, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative upstream inputs. RD-Agent is a research/automation agent that can act on prompts and API calls, so if Dagster-produced artifacts are consumed without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes Dagster-generated tables, metrics, or task specs without validation, incorrect upstream data can propagate.
IF RD-Agent is allowed to execute browser/API actions based on those inputs, the cascade can affect external systems.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Dagster and RD-Agent.
Require schema checks on all Dagster outputs.
Use a human approval gate for action-taking runs.
Log source provenance on every transferred artifact.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before RD-Agent acts.

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster is open-source and shows no residency or retention controls, while RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, logs, and secrets and uses third-party APIs such as OpenAI and Azure OpenAI. If regulated or sensitive data flows from Dagster into RD-Agent, default egress can create compliance breach risk without user awareness. The other agent is not cited for residency because none is documented.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or confidential financial data is routed into RD-Agent APIs, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to logs or prompts, RD-Agent’s external API usage can conflict with them.
mitigations: Block regulated data from RD-Agent prompts.
Use a DPA-approved deployment only.
Rotate and scope API keys narrowly.
Minimize logging of sensitive inputs.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls in the pipeline.
